Textile Materials Made from Polyolefins ( Excluding Cordage ) Sectional Committee, TX23 



FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard ( Second Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after 
the draft finalized by the Textile Materials Made from Polyolefins ( Excluding Cordage ) 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. 

This standard was first published in 1971 and subsequently revised in 1984. It has been revised 
again on the basis of experience gained in its implementation. Following are the major changes 
carried out in this revision; ,i 

a) The requirement of minimum elongation of the tape has been reduced, and 

b) The tolerance on width has been specified. 

The monoaxially oriented tape is a film in which the polymer is stretched at elevated temperature 
and by doing so, the linear coupling of the polymer molecules is oriented in longitudinal direction 
resulting in considerably improved tensile strength in that direction combined with low mass per 
unit area. These tapes are used in the manufacture of woven fabrics. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, 
the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the results of a test, shal be rounded off in 
accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values {revis^edy. The number 
of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified 
value in this standard. 



IS 6192 : 1994 



Indian Standard 

TEXTILES — MONOAXIALLY ORIENTED HIGH 

DENSITY POLYETHYLENE TAPES — 

SPECIFICATION 

( Second Revision ) 



1 SCOPE 

This standard prescribes the requirements for 
monoaxially oriented high density polyethylene 
tapes suitable for weaving. 

2 REFERENCES 

The following Indian Standards are necessary 
adjuncts to this standard: 

IS No, Title 

2454 : 1985 Method for determination of 

colour fastness of textile mate- 
rials to artificial light ( xenon 
lamp ) {first revision ) 

6193 : 1971 Methods of tests for monoaxi- 

ally oriented high density 
polyethylene/polypropylene 

tapes 

7328 : 1974 Specification for high density 

polyethylene materials for 
moulding and extrusion 

3 TERMINOLOGY 

3,1 High Density Polyethylene Tape 

A flat polyethylene tape having a high ratio of 
width to thickness and density ranging from 
0-940 to 0-965 g/-ml. 

NOTE — The method for production of these tapes 
include the slitting of fihn made by blown film or 
cast film process, stretching the slit film ia hot water 
or hot air or hot plate at 90°C to IIS^'C at a ratio of 
1 : 7 to 1 : 9, passing through a stabilization chamber 
for effecting a shrinkage of 3 to 4 percent and then 
winding over a package under uniform tension. 
The hot stretching process confers monoaxial 
orientation imparting high longitudinal strength. 

4 MATERIAL 

The tape shall be made from polyethylene 
having a density 0-940 to 965 g/ml ( see also 
IS 7328 :J974). The grade of polyethylene 
used for the manufacture of film shall be selec- 
ted taking into consideration the process used. 

5 REQUIREMENTS 

5.0 The tape shall conform to the requirements 
specified in 5.1 to 5.6 when tested by the 
methods given in IS 6193 : 1971. 



5.1 The minimum linear density of the tape- 
shall be 66-6 tex ( 600 denier ). 

5.2 The tenacity of the tapes shall not be less 
than 36 g/tex ( 4 g/denier ). 

5.3 The elongation of the tape at the point of 
rupture shall not be less than 15 percent. 

5.4 Width 

The finished width of the tape shall be as agreed 
to between the buyer and the seller or as 
declared. However, the finished width shall 
not exceed 5-0 mm and shall be subject to a 
tolerance of ±5 percent on agreed/declared 
width. 

5.5 The thickness of the tape shall correspond 
to the linear desity and width. 

5.6 Heat Shrinkage 

The heat shrinkage of the tape at 60*^0 shall 
not exceed 5 percent and shall not exceed 8 
percent at 95°C. For determining the shrinkage, 
the tape shall be subjected to the specified 
temperature for a period of 10 minutes in an 
air circulating oven and hot water bath 
respectively. 

5.7 In the case of pigmented tapes, the colour 
shall be fast to light and the colour fastness 
rating shall be 4 or better when tested by the 
method given in IS 2454 : 1985. 

6 MARKmC 

6.1 Each package of tape shall be tagged with a 
label containing the following information: 

a) Net mass ( when packed ); 

b) Width, mm; 

c) Thickness, p,m\ and 

d) Identification of the source of manu- 
facture. 

6.2 BIS Certification Marking 

The package may also be marked with the 
Standard Mark. 



IS 6192 ! 1994 



6.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed 
by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the rules and regula- 
tions made thereunder. The details of the 
conditions under which a licence for use of 
Standard Mark may be granted to manufac- 
turers or producers may be obtained from the 
Bureau of Indian Standards. 

7 PACKING 

Packages of polyethylene tape shall be suitably 



packed 
seller. 



as agreed between the buyer and the 



8 SAMPLING 

The number of samples to be tested for checking 
the conformity of the lot to the requirements 
of the standard shall be as specified in IS 6193 : 
1971. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to 
promote harmoious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality 
certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BUS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced 
in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, 
in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type 
or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director 
( Publications ), BIS. 

Reyision of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards 
are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review 
indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken 
up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the 
latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of *BIS Handbook' and 'Standards 
Monthly Addition'.
